headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading errors: Botpress can ingest/emit content while Transformers has broad shell, filesystem, and network powers.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent with no isolation surfaces documented, while Transformers can read/write files and run browsers/subprocesses. A shared workspace or file handoff would let attacker-controlled content from Botpress influence Transformers, but the pair does not document a default bridge, so this stays medium.
conditions: IF Botpress output is copied into a file or prompt that Transformers consumes
IF both agents share a writable workspace or message queue
mitigations: Separate their workspaces and disable shared folders
Require manual review before Transformers consumes Botpress output
Strip instructions from Botpress-generated text before reuse
Use provenance tags on any Botpress-to-Transformers handoff
requires-engineering: add an allowlist parser for trusted fields only

B_data_leakage.rationale: Transformers can read the filesystem and has broad network egress, so any sensitive files in a shared workspace could be exposed if Botpress writes or references them. Botpress itself shows no data classes touched, so the leakage path is inferred rather than directly evidenced, keeping this at medium.
conditions: IF Botpress stores user content in a shared directory
IF Transformers is pointed at that directory or receives those files as input
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of any shared directory
Disable network egress for Transformers during shared-data runs
Use per-agent service accounts with separate storage
Review and redact files before Transformers reads them
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs and DLP scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Transformers has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and broad network egress; Botpress can install packages. If both operate on the same directory or environment, concurrent writes and package changes can corrupt state or overwrite each other. The profiles document overlapping mutable capabilities, so the conflict is high.
conditions: IF both agents share the same writable directory
IF package installation targets the same environment or lockfile
mitigations: Run each agent in its own container or venv
Freeze package installs during shared runs
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Assign separate output directories
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress is a chatbot-style agent and Transformers is a document-processing stack with stdin/stdout and API/file surfaces. If Botpress output is fed into Transformers without verification, Transformers may treat generated text as authoritative and propagate errors downstream, but no direct action-taking authority is documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Botpress-generated text is used as input to Transformers without validation
IF Transformers output is consumed by another system as facts or instructions
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Require schema validation on Botpress outputs
Mark Botpress text as untrusted in prompts
Compare outputs against source documents before acting
requires-engineering: add citation and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Botpress exposes no touched data classes, and Transformers lists general data types but no compliance-specific constraints, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF future documentation shows a regulated data class flowing through either agent
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter residency or retention policy than the other
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Map retention settings before deployment
Separate regulated workloads from general workloads
